correctness.rationale: PASS: Matching polytope inequalities for odd C_n comprise n lower facets, n degree facets and one global blossom facet. For every odd n≥5 the fractional relaxation has a unique h>0 root of F_n(h)=avg h(h+2)/[2(h+1+cos θ_j)]=1; positivity and strict monotonicity yield root uniqueness, with h>1 from Poisson-root filter F_n(1)<√3/2. Fourier diagonalizes Q^{-1}=(h+2)/h[2(h+1)I+A_n], producing center t=1/(h+2), q0=t², and 2(q0+q1)=(1−2t)²; contact weights 2t and 1−2t give the full two John identities and global uniqueness on the fractional polytope. Blossom clearance is δ_n=(n−1)/2−n/(h+2)−√(nh/2)/(h+2). For odd n≥7, h>1 and (n−3)/2≥√(n/2) give strict δ_n>0, so the fractional optimum is the integral matching optimum with exactly 2n contacts. For n=5, displayed t=(21−√6)/60 and positive a,b,d give Q^{-1}=aI+b(2I+A_5)+dJ, exact support equalities q0=t², 2(q0+q1)=(1−2t)², 1ᵀQ1=(2−5t)²; positive weights at all 11 facets prove John optimality/uniqueness and nonzero d proves genuine blossom effect. Independent SymPy radical identities, finite Fourier checks for odd 7≤n≤71 and clearances pass; all-n step is analytic.

originality.rationale: PASS (best-of-knowledge): Published full Resultary fractional odd-cycle stable-set John ellipsoid exactly covers the relaxation x_i≥0,x_i+x_{i+1}≤1, but its assumptions explicitly exclude the odd-set/blossom inequality of the integral matching polytope. For n≥7, a nontrivial strict support-function inequality must be established to transfer it, and for n=5 its optimum is replaced by explicit rank-one correction. Published general vertex/edge-transitive fractional matching ellipsoid likewise omits integer blossom facets. Related integral matching-polytopes papers study Ehrhart/Gorenstein or circuit geometry, not the John contact transition. Hence fractional formula is prior-covered background; claimed new part is integral pentagonal exception and all higher-cycle screening.
